title: Streaming tool handshake observability checklist
content:
Purpose
This is a practical working checklist for the Hosted API teams (product, SDK, and observability) to ensure streaming tool-handshake flows are instrumented, debuggable, and safe in production. Focus is on the handshake phase (negotiation + metadata exchange) and the early streaming window where most client confusion and failures happen.

Context and constraints
- We support a progressive streaming API where a client can: open a session, negotiate tool capabilities, receive partial/typed outputs, and then invoke tool actions.
- Customers have reported two classes of production issues: (1) failed handshakes that leave "hung" client SDKs and (2) opaque errors during the first N tokens of a stream.
- Observability must be lightweight (low cardinailty by default), but provide deep-dive signals when enabled.

Non-goals
- Not a full PRD for new protocol changes. This is an ops+SDK checklist to be used alongside the protocol PRD.

Checklist: handshake lifecycle events (required)
- CLIENT: handshake.initiated – emitted when client opens stream and sends initial capability set.
- SERVER: handshake.received – first server ack that initial message parsed. Include parsing_time_ms.
- SERVER: handshake.validated – server validated tools and permissions; include tool_set_hash and allowed_tools_count. (sampled at 1% by default)
- SERVER: handshake.failed – canonical failure event with failure_reason (token_malformed | auth_denied | incompatible_tools | quota_exceeded), server_error_code, and user_visible_hint. Log at ERROR level.
- CLIENT/SERVER: handshake.completed – final state with negotiation_latency_ms and selected_tool_profile_id.

What to include in event payloads (keep flat, avoid embedding long objects)
- session_id (opaque UUID)
- request_id (traceable across logs)
- user_tier (free|paid|enterprise)
- client_sdk (name+semver)
- server_model_variant (short id)
- tool_set_hash (short fingerprint)
- negotiation_latency_ms (int)
- failure_reason (short token)
- sample_rate (if event is sampled)
- trace_url (link to trace/span in tracing system)

Telemetry levels and sampling guidance
- DEFAULT (low-cost): emit handshake.initiated, handshake.completed (1:100 sampling for completed for free tier; 1:10 for paid), and handshake.failed (no sampling).
- DEBUG (developer mode): full verbatim payloads, all validation steps, body previews (redacted). Enabled by SDK opt-in or account-level flag.
- ENTERPRISE (high-fidelity): 1:1 sampling for handshakes + attach first-50-tokens snapshot and tool metadata (obfuscated). Controlled via tenant config.

Metrics to derive (aggregated time series)
- handshake_success_rate = completed / initiated over 5m windows (by region, model_variant, sdk).
- handshake_error_rate_by_reason (top reasons heatmap).
- negotiation_latency_p50/p95/p999 (only store p999 when debug sampling enabled).
- concurrent_incomplete_handshakes (gauge) – useful for detecting hung clients.

Logs and structured traces
- Structured logs should use the event keys above and be compatible with our log schema.
- Tracing spans: handshake root span should include child spans for "parse_input", "validate_tools", "authorize", "select_variant", "prepare_stream". Each span should propagate request_id and session_id.
- For failed handshakes attach the short trace_url in the log entry.

SDK ergonomics: client-side behaviors to instrument and enforce
- Client should emit handshake.initiated immediately after opening connection. If not seen by server within X ms, server should emit handshake.timed_out and close.
- SDK should provide a developer-visible callback for "onHandshakeTimeout" with clear resolution steps.
- Backoff + retry: For transient server errors (5xx) during handshake, SDK should retry up to 2 times with jittered exponential backoff and emit retry.attempt events. Always include original_request_id on retries.
- Client must surface failure_reason and user_visible_hint in the top-level error object returned by the SDK. Avoid leaking internal error codes.

Structured output and validation guidance
- The handshake must negotiate an output schema id when the model will produce structured frames (e.g., JSON-LD snippets, typed deltas). The event "handshake.completed" should include negotiated_schema_id.
- On the server side, validate the schema against a lightweight schema registry (versioned). Emit schema_mismatch events with schema_registry_version.
- SDKs should expose a typed parser (auto-generated for known schemas) and fall back to safe-string mode with a warning telemetry event when parsing fails.

Observability pain points and mitigations
- Pain: High-cardinality tool metadata (tool URLs, long command strings) blowing up logs. Mitigation: hash tool_set for metrics and include only human-readable names in sampled debug logs.
- Pain: Clients stuck in "optimistic streaming" state where SDK shows spinner indefinitely. Mitigation: add concurrent_incomplete_handshakes metric + server-side watchdog that emits handshake.abandoned and emits user metric when threshold exceeded.
- Pain: Too many "false positive" failed handshakes from SDK bug. Mitigation: add client SDK-version bucketing in dashboards and enable 1:1 sampling for the bad SDK version when error-rate spikes.

Security and PII handling
- Never log full tool credentials or secrets. If client sends API keys to negotiate tools, the server should redact and emit handshake.credential_redacted with redaction_hash.
- Tokenization: redact first-party tokens except last 4 chars for debugging (configurable).

Alerting and dashboards (ops suggestions)
- Alert if handshake_success_rate < 98% over 5m for enterprise accounts.
- Alert on a sudden shift in dominant failure_reason (e.g., auth_denied spikes).
- Dashboard widgets: handshake funnel (initiated -> received -> validated -> completed), top failure reasons, negotiation latency histogram.

Developer experience / debug tooling
- "Replay" support: capture the minimal reproducible payload (session_id, initial_client_payload, tool_set_hash, selected_variant) for handshakes that failed and allow a developer replay endpoint in staging.
- Client-side devtools: SDK should expose a dev-mode UI hook that renders handshake timeline and last 200 bytes of the stream (redacted).

Open questions / decisions to make
- Should negotiation results be cacheable by tool_set_hash? Pros: faster response; Cons: consistency/permissions risk. (Action: product & security to evaluate by 2024-12-12)
- Exact sampling rates for paid vs enterprise tiers (Action: observability to propose numbers and cost impact analysis)
- Do we accept third-party tool manifests inline during handshake or require server-side fetch? Security prefers server fetch. (Action: security + product to finalize)

Next steps / owners
- Observability: implement handshake.* event schema and dashboard templates (owner: Hannah Lee, due 2024-12-20).
- SDK: add callouts for onHandshakeTimeout, retry telemetry, and dev-mode hook (owner: Diego Morales, due 2025-01-10).
- Product/security: finalize cache policy and third-party manifest handling (owner: Priya Nair & Omar Khan, due 2024-12-12).

Notes to self / rough snippets
- Example event line (structured log):
  { session_id: "s-...", request_id: "r-...", event: "handshake.received", parsing_time_ms: 12, client_sdk: "js/1.8.2" }
- Example error reason enums: auth_denied, invalid_tool_manifest, incompatible_schema, quota_exceeded, parse_error

References
- see CONFLUENCE-1234 for protocol draft and handshaking wire examples
- github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api-sdk (dev branch) for SDK hooks

-- end of checklist --

Unresolved: keep this doc lightweight and shareable with infra & security for quick reviews. Will spin a full PRD if changes to wire format are needed.
